answer: An operator leases one numbered stilling well on an estuary gauge. Only that holder may lower a sealed, mill-stamped kernel bag whose dyed seed mass and stain map were filed at signup, when the published tide hits the flood mark. The clock camera records a one-shot ripple train on the stilling basin. Graders match well number, bag serial, stain map, and ripple period to the template. A shared well, a borrowed bag, or a drop off the stand is merged into one farm. Fielding N aliases costs N charted wells, N distinct kernel lots, and N attendants at the same tide, which one skiff cannot cover.
